A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same confidence-estimation framework. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equation and Appendix A are readable and support reliable matching across versions.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original confidence-estimation comparisons, feature rankings and cross-LLM transfer results on four question-answering datasets.

after.justification: Section 4 retains the question-answering experiments and adds summarization results. Appendix A also reports original perturbation-entailment and training-sample analyses.

M1.justification: The six perturbations, semantic-set and ROUGE features, 0.3 labeling threshold and logistic regression estimator are retained. Renaming syntactic similarity to lexical similarity and specifying sentence selection and negation handling do not establish a changed underlying procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds CNN Daily Mail and XSUM summarization to the retained CoQA, SQuAD, TriviaQA and Natural Questions evaluations. This substantially broadens task coverage beyond question answering.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 retain the same five confidence-estimation comparators: number of semantic sets, lexical similarity, EigenValue, Eccentricity and Degree. The same comparator set is evaluated on the added summarization datasets.

E3.justification: The existing Q&A splits, main 1,000-example training budget, prompting and AUROC/AUARC evaluation remain unchanged. Added experiments introduce BART-large/Pegasus-large with reported 4,000-point summarization validation subsets, 250/500-example training budgets, and an entailment-based perturbation check.

E4.justification: New Appendix Tables 7 and 8 examine whether perturbations preserve prompt meaning on SQuAD and how training-data requirements affect performance on three Q&A datasets. Tables 4–6 also extend feature-importance and cross-model transfer analyses to summarization, substantially broadening the analytical evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions state that all results are averaged over three runs. Neither reports additional seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 2–6 add summarization scores, rankings and transfer results. CNN/Pegasus achieves AUROC/AUARC of 0.77/0.74; BART's 0.57 AUROC trails lexical similarity on CNN and XSUM, at 0.60 and 0.59 respectively. Retained CoQA–Mistral AUARC entries change from 0.49 to 0.61 in Tables 3 and 6 without explanation. Appendix Tables 7–8 add entailment percentages and training-size results.

T1.justification: Equation 1's conditional correctness probability and the mathematical content of the feature and label definitions are retained. Neither version supplies theorems or proofs, and v2 adds no substantive formal derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract and Discussion now explicitly claim effectiveness for summarization with Pegasus and BART alongside Q&A. The central contributions remain an extensible, interpretable framework requiring black-box access and confidence-model transfer across LLMs.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new appendix tests as supporting semantic preservation and effectiveness with fewer training examples, extends the order/redundancy-bias interpretation to summarization, and links future features to cross-dataset transfer. The existing supervision, English-only and ROUGE limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly identifies deberta-large-nli for entailment and specifies the sentence-selection rule for SP and preservation of negative words during stopword removal. These improve implementation disclosure. Existing hardware information, Q&A prompts and baseline-code access are retained.

R1.justification: Six references are added for DeBERTa, BART, Pegasus and the summarization datasets. Section 2's positioning against prior uncertainty-estimation approaches remains substantively unchanged; expanded author names in retained references are bibliographic presentation edits.

P1.justification: v2 standardizes model capitalization, changes syntactic to lexical similarity in the prose and tables, shortens future-work discussion, and moves Appendix A after the references. Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 2–6 gain summarization rows and are reflowed, while Tables 7–8 are newly added. Existing table formats remain recognizable. Figure 1 retains its workflow but uses a lower-resolution image with visibly less sharp text.

improvement.justification: The summarization experiments and Tables 7–8 strengthen empirical support for applicability, semantic preservation and training-data requirements; added implementation details also help reproducibility. These provide useful extensions to the retained study. Figure 1 is less legible and the CoQA–Mistral AUARC revision is unexplained, but the additional validation supports a limited net improvement.
